completion_data.completion_summary: Completed Phases 1-5 of the deploy-engine consolidation (scratch-tree regression harness, table-driven copier collapse, force/resync mode with manager.resync_all, preserved-state snapshot/restore, and a corrected regenerate/wipe sequence), plus the highest-risk half of Phase 6 (deploy-headless.sh rewritten with a bootstrap-safe default and a --wipe flag). memory_candidates.content: In this repo's deploy-engine (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/), manager.resync_all only resyncs extensions already marked 'active' in a target repo's project-root .claude-extensions.json state file. The historical glob-based load_all_globally engine (retired) was stateless and never wrote that file, so any target repo only ever deployed via the old engine has NO active-extension entries. A bulk-resync entry point (e.g. deploy-headless.sh's default invocation) must therefore force-load the baseline extension (e.g. 'core') first via manager.load(name, {force=true}) before calling resync_all, or it silently deploys zero files on first use against such a repo. Verified empirically: a bare resync_all against a from-scratch scratch git repo deployed 0 files; force-load-core-then-resync_all deployed 339.

test-deploy-propagation.sh (and similarly-shaped deploy-tree-first/source-store-fallback test harnesses) resolve deploy-headless.sh from the DEPLOYED copy (.claude/scripts/...) before falling back to the source-store copy (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/...). Editing only the source-store script does not make such a harness observe the fix -- a redeploy of the repo's own .claude/ tree is required first. Running the repo's own deploy mechanism against itself (e.g. bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/deploy-headless.sh <repo-root>) to refresh .claude/ is a SANCTIONED use of the deploy mechanism, not a hand-edit violation of the source-store/deploy-boundary rule, since .claude/ is fully gitignored and the deploy process writing the entire tree by design is explicitly exempted.

settings_backup.lua's helpers.ensure_directory (a thin wrapper over vim.fn.mkdir) can THROW a Lua error rather than return false when directory creation fails (e.g. a plain file already occupies the target path) -- discovered while testing manager.wipe's 'refuse to wipe when the snapshot step reports failure' requirement. Any caller relying on settings_backup.backup's documented (boolean, table) return contract to detect failure gracefully must pcall the call, since some of its underlying failure modes bypass that contract entirely and propagate as uncaught errors instead.
